integrity: Domination reduces exactly to hitting each core-leaf pair. For a block partition, union dominance becomes a two-vertex-cover condition on the block incidence multigraph. Every block belongs to a two-cover but no singleton is a cover. A pigeonhole argument excludes at least five blocks. Four-block incidence supports are exactly 2K2, P4 and C4. Surjective assignments of private pairs to the support edges, with orientations and automorphism quotients, yield an exact optimum-partition count. Direct full partition enumerations for n=2..5 and graph adjacency checks corroborate the argument.
scientific_limitations: The core is a finite simple graph of order at least two; connectivity is not assumed.
Every core vertex is attached to exactly one private leaf; larger or mixed attachments are outside scope.
The enumeration counts unordered vertex-set partitions of the fixed labeled corona, not graph-automorphism orbits.
The result concerns ordinary coalition partitions, not connected coalition partitions.
Only sizes n=2 to n=5 are exhaustively enumerated computationally; the proof covers arbitrary n.
Undiscovered equivalent results in unindexed or differently phrased literature remain possible.
title: Coalition partitions of leaf coronas and their incidence types
